value.rationale: A natural finite Allee-rescue question asks what habitat size maximizes the probability that two founders reach a finite population threshold. The theorem supplies a nontrivial exact first optimizer switch and an all-K capacity bound, not just a plot or numerical sample. Its assumption of well-mixed independent draws limits practical extrapolation without erasing its structural model value.

final_claim: For K>=3, all optimizer capacities of the specified two-founder finite cooperative birth-death recovery event lie K<=L<=2K-3; K=3,4 uniquely favor L=K; for K=5 the unique optimal L switches 5 to 6 at gamma=(113+sqrt23901)/253 (tie exactly at threshold).
limitations: Model has independent with-replacement mate/nursery draws and finite first-hit objective; spatial models and population persistence are different.
No exhaustive search of all indexed ecological birth-death sources; some full texts not inspected.
